text:
Vancouver is 6-20-1 with 13 points and, by our numbers, essentially no path to the playoffs. This is not bad luck. The Canucks get 40.4% of expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets) and 41% at five on five, both the kind of numbers that lose games, and they have also allowed almost 14 more goals than those chances predict. Kevin Lankinen is 0-4-0 at .833 over his last five starts. The New York Times called it Vancouver's mess in net.

Manny Malhotra, hired in June after Adam Foote was fired, is coaching a team that is selling. Max Sasson went to the Rangers. Brock Boeser, having a career year and top 25 in scoring according to BVM Sports, is in trade chat in The Province, and Filip Hronek is in the rumor columns too. GM Ryan Johnson spoke at the quarter mark. Sportsnaut reported attendance at a 25-year low.

The worst news is Elias Pettersson, who missed practice and is set to see a specialist on the road trip, per The Province, with what Daily Hive called a murky update from the GM. The Hronek and Zeev Buium pair has taken only 33% of the chances. The young pieces worth following are Buium, Tom Willander, Jonathan Lekkerimäki and Liam Ohgren. Paul Cotter ended a 21-game goal drought in Detroit and Cole Reinhardt got his first point as a Canuck. Small things, but this season is now about small things.
headline: The Canucks have hit bottom, and the sale is on
